chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Give glad tidings of Paradise to the humble: Burayd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli, Abu Basir Layth ibn al-Bukhtari al-Muradi, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Zurara. Four possessors of nobility and the trustees of Allah upon His Halal and Haram, if it were not for these four, the traces of prophethood would have been cut off and erased.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four trustees of Allah mentioned in Rijal al-Kashshi who preserve the traces of prophethood?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi highlights the four 'Nujaba' (noble ones) as the primary transmitters who preserved the Sunnah during the Minor Occultation, ensuring the continuity of prophetic authority. Their role as 'trustees of Allah' underscores the Shia concept of their infallible-like precision in distinguishing between Halal and Haram, making them the living link to the Prophet's teachings.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/158] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh b. Nusayr from Ya`qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Jamil b. Darraj who said:

I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: give glad tidings of paradise to the humble: Burayd b. Muawiya al-Ijli, Abu Basir Layth b. al-Bukhtari al-Muradi, Muhammad b. Muslim and Zurara. Four possessors of nobility and the trustees of Allah upon his Halal and Haram, if it wasn’t for them the traces of prophethood would have perished and been destroyed.
